Lab meeting06

Why restructure the pipeline?

Severe channels enter reference / ICA
Identify persistent channels and large transients earlier
Fixed PCA = 20
Use measured rank and record its basis
Training quality conflated with output quality
Separate ICA training from analysis and final QC
Mask restoration and recovery are opaque
Preserve sample maps, original events, and missing intervals
Lab meeting07

v2 processing structure

1Audit raw values and reference
2Combine channel detectors; record reasons
3Mark extreme transients before filtering
4Create analysis and ICA-training branches
5Fixed compatible reference; fit ICA on accepted samples
6Transfer ICA; recheck residual artifacts
7Interpolate; restore original time axis and events
Rejected intervals remain gaps on the original clock.
Lab meeting08

Complementary channel detection

PREP detection copy
1 Hz high-pass; full bad-channel list
Amplitude and output-band checks
Persistent extremes and frequency-dependent residuals
Teacher clean_channels detector
Correlation threshold 0.8; moved before reference / ICA
Keep per-channel evidence; do not assume one detector catches every artifact.
Lab meeting09

ICA training and analysis are separate branches

ICA training

  • 1–45 Hz
  • Accepted training samples
  • Measured rank; seed 0

Analysis output

  • 0.1–45 Hz
  • Same channel order and reference
  • Apply ICA; assess residuals again
Lab meeting10

ICA classification and human review

P(Muscle) + P(Eye) + P(Heart) + P(Line Noise) + P(Channel Noise) ≥ 0.90
  • Other is excluded from this sum.
  • Inspect scalp maps, spectra and component time courses.
  • sub17 and sub18: no IC crossed this automatic threshold.
No automatic rejection does not mean no residual artifact.

Lab meeting13

What the common QC gates measure

Continuous candidates
Original nonoverlapping 2-s windows; all 64 final channels finite; absolute voltage ≤150 µV.
S4 candidates
−1 to +2 s; baseline −1000 to 0 ms, then the same amplitude gate. 90 candidates per person.
Local repair
75 accepted windows actually repaired; 280 is a separate repair-branch total.
Different filters, reference, ICA and interpolation: descriptive QC, not validated neural preservation.

Lab meeting21

Candidate SOP for TRF and PPC

Shared foundation
Input audit; channel reasons; compatible ICA; preserved clock and masks
TRF branch
Valid speech segments; no lag embedding across gaps; filter/resampling edges
PPC branch
Identified single trials; matched items; phase reference and padding
Separate local ERP repair
Development control only until phase effects are validated
Recommendation: validate the v2 structure; retain the teacher pipeline as a comparator.

Lab meeting25

Event identity and acoustic timing

  • Both presentations send code 1; recover poem identity and presentation from logs and sequence.
  • Playback failure can still leave markers; trigger time is not acoustic onset.
  • Keep trigger_onset and acoustic_onset separate; audit latency, jitter and drift.
The actual acquisition version must be matched to each recording.
Lab meeting26

TRF implementation workflow

1Audit actual audio + existing features
2Align features and EEG
3Create valid material-level folds
4Inner CV: select ridge regularization
5Outer CV: predict held-out EEG
6Aggregate a participant-level endpoint
Lab meeting27

Keep repeated material in the same outer fold

Schematic: both presentations stay in the same material cell.

The test material is held out before parameter tuning.
Lab meeting28

TRF folds: implementation rules

  • Keep both presentations of a poem in the same outer fold.
  • Never randomly split neighboring samples or create lags across NaNs/material boundaries.
  • Fit standardization and choose ridge parameters inside training data only.
All feature-model comparisons use the same held-out intervals.
Lab meeting29

H1 endpoint: one value per participant

r(test fold × ROI channel) → Fisher z = atanh(r) → prespecified summary
  • Freeze ROI, frequency band, lag window and fold weighting.
  • Decide equal-material or duration weighting in advance.
  • Folds and electrodes do not increase participant n.
Lab meeting30

H1 inference: the ASD–TD performance difference

Encoding z ~ Group + Age term + Sex + Prespecified quality terms
  • Primary estimand: adjusted Group coefficient on the z scale.
  • Show raw participant values and the unadjusted contrast.
  • Report effect size, 95% CI and exact raw/adjusted P.
Lab meeting31

Model detectability and group inference are different tests

Within-participant null
Shift/block controls preserve time structure; assess whether the model identifies stimulus-related information
Between-group H1
Compare the frozen participant summaries using the planned group model
No result-based exclusion
Do not remove a person merely for failing their individual null test
Lab meeting32

H2 statistical interface

ΔPPC = PPC(second) − PPC(first)
  • Primary contrast: mean(ΔPPC in ASD) − mean(ΔPPC in TD).
  • Use participant-level change scores with frozen adjustment.
  • Test the difference in change, not separate within-group significance.
Lab meeting33

One primary family: H1 and H2

  • Two-sided family-wise α = 0.05.
  • Sort the two primary raw P values.
  • First threshold: 0.025; second: 0.05, with sequential stopping.
  • Report raw and Holm-adjusted P values.
Do not replace a failed or unestimable primary endpoint with a secondary outcome.
Lab meeting34

Secondary TRF questions need controlled contrasts

Acoustic baseline
Freeze envelope, onset or spectral controls.
Linguistic extension
Add reliable phoneme, syllable or word features.
Matched evaluation
Same test materials; separate inner tuning.
Timecourse follow-up
Prespecified ROI/windows; corrected field exploration.
A difference in prediction correlation is not uniquely explained variance.
Lab meeting35

Missing endpoints, precision and sensitivity

Actual sample size
Report endpoint-specific n and exclusion reasons by group
Missing values
Never fill a missing EEG endpoint with zero
Quality sensitivity
Prespecify duration/material matching, reference, age overlap and influence checks
Interpret uncertainty
No guaranteed power at 20/group; nonsignificance is not equivalence
